candidates.statement: Under scenario 1.1, the Geriatric Use subsection must include the percentage of patients 65 156 years of age and older and the percentage of patients 75 years of age and older (or the total 157 number of patients 65 years of age and older and the total number of patients 75 years of age and 158 older) in the clinical studies of the drug. 29 Under this scenario, to provide more information to 159 health care practitioners about geriatric exposure, the FDA recommends that this subsection 160 present both the number and percentage of drug-exposed patients 65 years of age and older, and 161 the number and percentage of drug-exposed patients 75 years of age and older in a defined group 162 of clinical studies (typically the clinical studies that supported the approval of the drug in adult 163 patients, including geriatric patients). Under scenario 1.1, alternative age cutoff point(s) within 164 the geriatric population may be permitted to describe drug exposure, if the FDA determines that 165 such age cutoff point(s) are accurate and appropriate. 30
candidates.context: Information in this subsection is typically derived from results from controlled clinical studies 149 submitted in the application or supplement(s) that are relevant to the use of the drug in geriatric 150 patients. candidates.statement: The Geriatric Use subsection must contain a summary of observed differences or specific 280 monitoring or dosage requirements in certain situations. 35 These situations occur when clinical 281 studies and/or other reported clinical experience indicate that the use of the drug in geriatric 282 patients, compared to its use in younger adult patients, is associated with differences in safety or 283 effectiveness or requires specific monitoring or different recommended dosage in geriatric 284 patients. candidates.statement: 69 The BOXED WARNING section requires that certain contraindications or serious warnings may be required by the FDA to be presented in a box (21 CFR 201.57(c)(1)). The WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS “section must describe clinically significant adverse reactions (including any that are potentially fatal, are serious even if infrequent, or can be prevented or mitigated through appropriate use of the drug), other potential safety hazards” (21 CFR 201.57(c)(6)(i)). The CONTRAINDICATIONS “section must describe any situations in which the drug should not be used because the risk of use (e.g., certain potentially fatal adverse reactions) clearly outweighs any possible therapeutic benefit … Known hazards and not theoretical possibilities must be listed” (21 CFR 201.57(c)(5)).
